answer: Reciprocal edge aging scores agents by links that are bidirectional and survive multiple epochs. An edge counts only if both endpoints answer liveness probes, so a fresh onyx mark from a one-off peer adds nothing. Old graph relic edges are pruned unless refreshed, and each surviving thread must route through independent neighborhoods. An attacker pays continuous uptime, probe response, and link-maintenance cost per sybil; fake clusters fail because internal edges never reach independent agents.
